title: Remote viewers locate the MX missile every week and the program is cancelled
summary: Joe McMoneagle tells of Remote viewers locate the MX missile every week and the program is cancelled, about late 1970s-1980s at Washington, D.C., and says they saw it or took part. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: we notified we we wrote a white paper it's called a white paper one paragraph We sent it to the Situation Room in the White House and said won't work why not because we can tell you where it is every time

plain: Joe McMoneagle says he worked as a remote viewer for the US government, meaning someone trained to describe faraway places or objects using only the mind. He says that from the late 1970s into the 1980s his group could find the MX, a new US nuclear missile whose location was meant to stay hidden, every week. They sent a one-paragraph white paper, a short official note, to the White House Situation Room, the president's crisis room, saying the plan would not work because they could tell where the missile was every time, and he says the programme was then cancelled. If true, it would mean the mind can beat military secrecy.
